title: How to Read a Python Error Message (Traceback Explained for Beginners)
description:
Python error messages look scary, but every one follows the same pattern. Read three real errors with me (NameError, TypeError and a ZeroDivisionError with a 3-step traceback) and learn the one habit that fixes most of them: start at the bottom line.

CHAPTERS
0:00 Errors follow a pattern
0:18 Error 1: NameError (read the last line first)
1:03 Error 2: TypeError
1:41 Error 3: a longer traceback
2:37 The 3-step method
2:57 Your turn

PRACTICE: break a working program on purpose (misspell a name, divide by zero) and read the traceback bottom-up before fixing it.

Watch next: Python If Else Explained for Beginners (elif, and/or, Common Mistakes)

Code in Small Steps: one useful Python idea at a time, with real code you can run. New lesson every week.
The presenter is an illustrated character and the voice is synthetic; every program and every output shown is real (Python 3.13).
